synopsis: The central recommendation is to complete scenario architecture, fleet-data pipelines, tools and credibility work before prototype arrival in mid-2027, so the roughly 16-week window becomes confirmation, calibration and discrepancy resolution rather than initial method development [f11643, f7379, f7593]. Campaign governance should separate failure-seeking discovery, frozen pre-registered performance estimation, and requirement/regression testing; discovery failure fractions must not be presented as field failure rates [f133, f6935, f6669]. The proposed architecture combines inexpensive high-volume testing with selected high-fidelity and physical checks, including a physical anchor campaign during the first six weeks after hardware delivery [f693, f8871, f13494]. Credibility requires safety-derived acceptance criteria agreed before the main campaign and advance reviewer agreement on evidence taxonomy and substitution rules, because internal engineering confidence does not guarantee an externally acceptable dossier [f11085, f11039, f1988]. Planning remains conditional: no published off-road precedent was found for compressing three or four years of validation into under four months, a working evidence factory rather than completed validation is judged realistic by mid-2027, and compute and result triage remain unbudgeted despite an illustrative four-month, ten-GPU cost of about USD 54,000 [f7350, f372, f10507, f8312]. The campaign should therefore initiate a living evidence base, with field near misses and newly encountered scenarios feeding subsequent validation [f11628, f724].
